nodes.label: Client-side reward sort (composite index workaround)
nodes.rationale: Rewards query is where('active'==true) only and sorted by pointsCost in JS. The original active+orderBy(pointsCost) needed a Firestore composite index that was never created, so the query failed silently and no rewards appeared on the card (fixed 26/10/2026, commit e531d04). Sorting client-side avoids depending on index deployment.

nodes.label: Hostname-aware white-label bootstrap
nodes.rationale: On a custom domain (card.washhub.it) the brand is applied synchronously in <head> before CSS loads: document.title, manifest (manifest-washhub.json), theme-color, apple-touch-icon/title and an injected <style> for body/.card-app gradient. Done this early so iOS 'Add to Home Screen' captures the merchant branding and there is no FidelAI flash. A second body IIFE fills merchant name/logo on DOMContentLoaded. Merchant Firestore ID is also resolved from the hostname (HOSTNAME_MERCHANTS) so NFC/short links need no ?m= param.

nodes.label: Redeem code flow (4-digit code, 5-min TTL)
nodes.rationale: Customer taps 'Riscatta' -> confirm() -> POST generateRedeemCode {merchant, customerId, rewardId} -> server returns {code, expiresAt, rewardName, pointsCost}. Code is shown full-screen with a live countdown so the cashier can type/read it at the till; points are deducted server-side when the operator confirms the code, not on the card. Closing the modal calls loadCard() to refresh points and history.

nodes.label: Card self-activation flow
nodes.rationale: If no customer id (?c= param or localStorage) or the customer doc has cardAttivata !== true, the activation form is shown instead of the card. Form POSTs {merchant slug, name, phone, email, consentPrivacy, consentSms, consentEmail} to the selfActivateCard Cloud Function (merchant slug from __hostBrands, falling back to Firestore merchantId). Privacy consent is mandatory, SMS/email marketing consents optional (GDPR fix 025a1dc). On success the normalised phone is stored as the customer id in localStorage and the page reloads with ?c=<phone>, so returning visitors on the same device open the card directly. Stale localStorage ids are cleared when the doc is missing/unactivated.

nodes.label: getDate
nodes.rationale: Tolerates three createdAt encodings (Firestore Timestamp with toDate, raw {seconds} object, ISO string) because merchants were created by different code paths over time.

nodes.label: getMerchantStatus
nodes.rationale: Status derivation: 'active' only when stripeSubscriptionId exists and stripeSubscriptionStatus === 'active'; 'trial' when createdAt is within TRIAL_DAYS (14) and there is no stripeSubscriptionId; everything else is 'expired'. Stripe is the source of truth for paid status, Firestore createdAt for trial window.

nodes.label: MRR / SaaS KPI computation
nodes.rationale: MRR = sum of PLAN_PRICES[plan] over merchants with status 'active' only; trials and expired contribute nothing. Plan defaults to 'starter' when missing. KPIs computed client-side from a full scan of the 'merchants' collection (acceptable at current scale, will not scale past a few thousand merchants).

nodes.label: Super Admin email gate
nodes.rationale: Admin panel authorisation is a single hard-coded email (ADMIN_EMAIL) compared client-side after Firebase email/password sign-in and again in onAuthStateChanged; any other user is signed out. No custom claims or Firestore role: it relies on Firestore rules to actually protect the 'merchants' collection read. Fragile: the gate is purely cosmetic if rules allow reads.
